headline: Committee advances emergency funding charter change, revisits notice proposals

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.voteItem: Motion to recommend passage on first reading of Resolution 2688 (emergency appropriations charter amendment), including non-substantive revisions
meeting.summary: The committee voted 8–0, with one member excused, to recommend Resolution 2688 on first reading. Members withdrew motions on deferred public meeting notice proposals after a deputy corporation counsel said a proposal conflicts with state law.
meeting.recap: The Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee reconvened on June 18th, 2026.[[0:05:30]] Resolution 2688 would ask voters to let the mayor, with council approval, make an emergency appropriation (spending approval) for a line of credit.[[0:10:55]] It would also say the 1% emergency spending limit does not cover money already in an emergency fund.[[0:11:10]] The committee voted 8–0 to recommend passing Resolution 2688 on first reading.[[0:18:05]] The committee returned to two deferred proposals on public meeting notices and how deadlines are counted.[[0:50:43]] A deputy corporation counsel (County lawyer) said the proposal conflicts with state law and should not go on the ballot as written.[[1:23:24]] Members withdrew their motions on these proposals, putting the committee back at square one.[[1:40:48]]
decided: The committee voted 8–0 to recommend passing Resolution 2688 on first reading, with one member excused.
meeting.next: The committee planned to go through all the deferred proposals and then decide which to prioritize for the ballot.

trackerIssues.title: Charter amendments headed to the general election ballot

issues.oneLine: A proposed charter change would make clear the 1% emergency spending limit does not cover money already in an emergency fund.
issues.why: The budget director said that after the recent Kona storms, the County had to come back for a second approval through two readings to fund recovery.

deadlines.t: Proposed effective date of the emergency appropriations charter change.

issues.brief: A council member said they expect more storm damage in the future and supported the change.[[#1]] The budget director said any use would list the emergency declarations that triggered it.[[#2]] The committee voted 8–0 to recommend passing Resolution 2688 on first reading.[[#3]]
